$comment: One committed JSON file under governance/decisions/, one decision. The
log is append-only: a decision is never edited in place once its
`status` leaves `"open"`. Correcting or reversing a decided record means
adding a NEW record whose `supersedes` names the old one's `id` -- the
old file stays, unchanged, as history. scripts/check-decision-records.mjs
is this contract's validator; it also flags an `"open"` record past its
`expiry` and a relaxation whose `sunset` has passed.
Matches the decision-tier rule at #1187 comment 5800142871 (tier-1:
independent second opinion, then act on consensus; tier-2: owner only)
and the Fable second opinion's point 6 ('Audit trail... decision records
belong in a committed, append-only governance/decisions/') and point 7
('add decision expiry with default-deny, an append-only committed
decision log, and a sunset on every relaxation').
requiredFieldsNote: Listed unconditionally below for a quick scan, but `decidedBy` and
`decision` are each required ONLY when `status` is `"decided"` -- see
`rule` below for the exact conditional wording. This list is
the real (conditional) validation and does not read this array.
rule: `id` is a short, stable, kebab-case identifier, unique across every file
in governance/decisions/, and MUST equal the record's own filename
without the `.json` extension (`governance/decisions/<id>.json`) --
scripts/check-decision-records.mjs rejects a mismatch. `tier` is
`"tier-1"` or `"tier-2"` per the decision-tier rule (#1187 comment
5800142871); a tier-0 action is, by that same rule, never recorded here
at all -- this log exists for decisions that needed a second opinion or
the owner, not for ordinary reversible work.
`question` is a one- or two-sentence statement of what was actually being
decided, written so a reader with no other context understands the
choice. `options` is a non-empty array of short strings naming the real
alternatives that were on the table (a decision with only one option was
not a decision). `recommendation` names which option the proposer
recommended, in the proposer's own words -- it may differ from
`decision` below when the deciding party did not simply rubber-stamp it.
`reviews` is an array, each entry `{ role, instance, provider, model,
effort, verdict, link }`: `role` is one of `author`, `primary`,
`secondary`, or `owner`; `instance` and `provider`/`model`/`effort` mirror
docs/contracts/review-record.json's identity fields (kept independent of
that schema on purpose -- a decision record is a durable artifact read
long after the reviewing PR's comments may be edited or the thread
archived, so it restates rather than references the identity facts it
needs); `verdict` is `approve`, `reject`, or `changes`; `link` is a URL
to the actual review (an issue comment, a PR review) where it happened.
`reviews` may be empty for a `decidedBy: "owner"` record made without a
prior agent recommendation (a pure business/priority call), but a
`tier-1` record decided by `"consensus"` is expected to carry at least
two entries whose verdicts are both `approve` and which are independent
in the same sense docs/contracts/review-record.json defines (distinct
`instance`, differing in `model` or `provider`).
`status` is `"open"` (proposed, not yet acted on), `"decided"` (acted
on -- the normal end state), or `"expired"` (an `"open"` record whose
`expiry` passed with no decision -- see below). `decidedBy` is `"owner"`
or `"consensus"`, matching the decision-tier rule's own two paths to
action; required whenever `status` is `"decided"`. `decision` is the
actual outcome in prose, naming which option (if any) was chosen, and is
required whenever `status` is `"decided"`.
`relaxesGateOrPolicy` is a required boolean with no default -- the same
fail-closed discipline packages/controller/src/review/types.ts's own
`ReviewPolicy.decisionUse` doc comment describes ('a silently-assumed
false would make an account's real requirement invisible'). The record's
own author declares it explicitly rather than scripts/check-decision-
records.mjs inferring it from `decision` prose, which would be exactly
the kind of guess this repository's conventions warn against. `true`
means this decision loosens a check, widens an exemption, or defers an
enforcement deadline; `false` means it does not (a new policy, a
tightening, a priority call, or a bug fix in a gate's own logic that
removes a false positive rather than a real safeguard all read `false`).
SELF-DECLARED, HONOUR SYSTEM (#1187 review at 8e6d97ea, should-fix 14):
nothing here or in scripts/check-decision-records.mjs verifies that a
record's own characterization of its change matches what the change
actually does -- a record CAN declare `false` to avoid the sunset
requirement while the linked change is, in substance, a relaxation.
docs/HITL.md's 'Honour-system limits' section says this plainly and
names it as the same class of gap as every other self-declared field on
this record. A record's own `decision` and `notes` prose should say, in
plain language, why `relaxesGateOrPolicy` was set the way it was --
'this removes a false positive, not a real safeguard' is a claim a
reader can check, 'this is not a relaxation' alone is not.
`expiry` is a required RFC 3339 date (or `null` only for a `"decided"`
record whose `relaxesGateOrPolicy` is `false`). ON EXPIRY THE DEFAULT IS
DENY: an `"open"` record whose `expiry` has passed and which was never
decided is flagged by scripts/check-decision-records.mjs as needing its
`status` corrected to `"expired"`; nothing in this repository ever
treats silence past expiry as approval. `sunset` is an RFC 3339 date,
REQUIRED when `relaxesGateOrPolicy` is `true` and forbidden (must be
`null`) when it is `false`; scripts/check-decision-records.mjs enforces
that pairing directly (no inference) and separately flags a `"decided"`
record whose `sunset` has passed without a superseding record renewing
it.
`supersedes` is an optional array of prior decision `id`s this record
replaces; a record named there is never deleted or edited, only
superseded (and never itself edited afterward either, whether or not
anything supersedes it -- see 'DECIDED RECORDS ARE IMMUTABLE' below).
`links` is optional: `{ pullRequests: string[], patchIds: string[],
issues: string[], paths: string[] }`, used by scripts/land-stack.mjs's
tier-2 gate (governance/review-tiers.json) to find the decision record
that authorizes a specific pull request or governance/model-
qualifications/ path. A `"decided"`, `decidedBy: "owner"`, `tier:
"tier-2"`, unexpired record satisfies that gate either by PR number or
by path glob, with a requirement on each:
- PR-SCOPED: `links.pullRequests` must name the PR, AND
`links.patchIds` must be a non-empty array containing the EXACT
(case-insensitive) `git patch-id --verbatim` of the pull request's own
net diff against its merge base -- a PR-scoped authorization with no
pinned patch-id at all authorizes NOTHING.
- PATH-SCOPED: `links.paths` globs (each checked against
`isOverbroadPathGlob` -- must be a literal path or exactly one of
`governance/review-tiers.json`'s own `tier2.globs` entries,
verbatim) must cover every tier-2 path the change touches, AND
`expiry` must be non-null -- a path-scoped authorization with
`expiry: null` would otherwise be a standing blank cheque,
pre-authorizing every future change under that glob forever from
one single owner decision.
`scripts/check-decision-records.mjs` enforces both requirements as
shape-validation findings on any record where `tier: "tier-2"` and
`status: "decided"` together.
PATCH-ID, NOT HEAD SHA (#1187 review round 5, blocking, reviewer 2): an
earlier version of this contract pinned `links.headShas` to the exact
head commit the owner reviewed. That pin is UNSATISFIABLE under this
repository's own strict, up-to-date branch protection on `main`: the
instant the decision record itself lands (which necessarily advances
`main`, since the record is committed there), every open pull request it
was meant to authorize becomes `BEHIND` and needs a restack before it can
merge -- which changes its head sha and breaks the pin, every single
time, by construction. `links.patchIds` instead pins the CONTENT of the
change: `git patch-id --verbatim` (NOT `--stable` -- #1187 review round
6, blocking, both reviewers: `--stable` ignores whitespace differences
when hashing, which would let a semantic whitespace-only edit to a
tier-2 YAML workflow or shell `run:` block keep an owner's
authorization; `--verbatim` does not ignore whitespace) hashes a diff in
a way that ignores LINE NUMBERS but DOES hash surrounding context, so it
survives a pure merge-forward from `main` or an ordinary restack ONLY
WHEN the base-branch changes involved do not touch a line within, or
immediately adjacent to, the pull request's own diff hunks -- verified
directly in a scratch repository (#1187 review round 6, both reviewers):
an unrelated-file or far-away-line base change leaves the patch-id
unchanged; a base change that reaches into the PR's own hunk context
changes it, correctly, because the merged content genuinely differs from
what was reviewed. An earlier version of this contract claimed the
patch-id survives EVERY restack unconditionally; that was too strong and
is corrected here. THE FLOW: the pull request opens and is reviewed at
some head; its patch-id against its merge base is computed and recorded
in a NEW decision record's `links.patchIds`; that record is committed
(landing through the merge train like any other tier-1 governance
change); the authorized pull request, now `BEHIND` because the record's
own commit advanced `main`, restacks (merge or rebase) onto the new
`main`; its head sha has changed, and `git patch-id --verbatim` of its
diff against the (possibly also-advanced) merge base is recomputed FRESH
at merge time by `scripts/land-stack.mjs`'s tier-2 gate (never trusted
from a value cached at review time) -- if the base-branch changes did
not reach the PR's own hunk context, it still matches `links.patchIds`
and the PR merges, carrying the authorization forward through the
restack it was itself forced into; if they did, the patch-id no longer
matches, the gate correctly refuses, and the owner authorizes a fresh
decision record against the new patch-id. A genuine content change to
the PR itself after the decision record landed also produces a
different patch-id and the gate refuses, exactly as a stale head-sha pin
was meant to. LIMITATION, DOCUMENTED RATHER THAN LEFT IMPLICIT: for a
merge-train BATCH pull request stacking several already-reviewed
constituent pull requests, `scripts/land-stack.mjs` checks the batch
PR's own single patch-id against its own single merge base; it does not
decompose the batch into per-constituent patch-ids and check each
constituent's authorization independently. In practice this still
requires the WHOLE batch's net diff to match some record's
`links.patchIds` verbatim, which a batch assembled from independently-
authorized constituents will not generally do -- batching several
tier-2 changes under one new decision record's patch-id, computed
against the actual batch, is the documented path today, the same class
of known, acknowledged gap as governance/review-tiers.json's own
merge-train batch-classification limitation.
DECIDED RECORDS ARE IMMUTABLE (#1187 review round 4, should-fix):
`scripts/land-stack.mjs`'s `evaluateChangedDecisionRecords` refuses a
pull request that changes the CONTENT of a record whose base-branch
version already has `status: "decided"` -- even a formatting-only
change is compared by parsed value, not raw text, so only a genuine
content edit trips this. The only sanctioned way to change a decided
record is a NEW record whose `supersedes` names the old one; the old
file itself is never touched again. A record still `"open"` on the
base branch may be freely edited -- it has not been decided yet, so
ordinary iteration is exactly what should happen.
`notes` is optional free-form prose for anything the fields above cannot
carry -- most commonly, on a backfilled record for a decision made
before this schema existed, a plain statement that the original
reviewing sessions' exact `instance`/`provider`/`model` identities were
not captured at the time and are reconstructed from the surviving
record (an issue or PR comment) rather than measured directly. A
backfilled `reviews[]` entry states this the same way: an honestly
labelled `instance` of `"unrecorded-predates-schema"` rather than an
invented value, per this repository's own rule that a position claimed
ahead of its evidence is a defect (docs/LIFECYCLE.md).
